column1: # Work bounds for tools/java-reference/run.sh route (J01.3), one row per fixture DSN.
# board       path under fixtures/ without .dsn (freerouting-dev bench also accepts the stem)
# max_passes  the batch autorouter's pass limit (autorouter.max_passes)
# max_items   optional autorouter.max_items (items routed over all passes); empty = no limit
# note        why the bound is what it is
# Route references run the autorouter only (optimizer off) and are bounded by work, never by
# time, so they are reproducible. The bounds were chosen on 2026-10-15/16 from one exploration
# run of every fixture at a773a70ec with max_passes 100 and a 60 s safety timeout (4 boards in
# parallel, on a machine at load 15-30 from other sessions, so the times are 2-5x a quiet run),
# plus a max_passes 1 run of the boards that did not finish pass 1 in 60 s:
# - a board that stopped on its own (all routed, or Java's stop rules) within 90 s keeps Java's
#   default of 100 passes: the bound never fires, and the reference is Java's natural result;
# - any other board gets the passes that fit in 45 s of measured pass time, but at least 3, so
#   the ripup and restore paths run on every board;
# - boards whose first pass alone took over a minute get 3 (pass 1 took 2-7 min there).
# - four boards that hit the 30 min safety timeout at load 25-30 got fewer passes (see their
#   notes); they were routed with a 2 h safety timeout, which their JSONs record.
# No board needs max_items at these pass limits. Measured 2026-10-16 at load 20-35 from other
# sessions: 18,223 s of routing summed over the 170 boards, 2 h 15 min wall in 3 parallel runs
# plus 26 min for the reruns. Expect a fraction of that on a quiet machine (the exploration's
# pass times were 2-5x those of a quiet run).
# A new fixture needs a row here before run.sh route will route it.
